findings.claim: PDF-by-URL is sent as {"type":"file","file":{"type":"input_file","file_url":...,"filename":"document.pdf"}} — a shape that does not exist in the Chat Completions API. The current OpenAI OpenAPI spec's ChatCompletionRequestMessageContentPartFile defines the `file` object with ONLY `filename`, `file_data`, `file_id`; there is no `file_url` field and no nested `type` discriminator (those belong to the Responses API's input_file part, which the engine had mixed in).
findings.evidence: Probe (scratch /probe, probe_pdf_url_shape via mock capture) → captured body part: "file|input_file|https://example.com/x.pdf|document.pdf|ABSENT(file_data)". Spec: openai-openapi@master openapi.yaml lines ~31077-31111: file properties = filename/file_data/file_id only. Code: ChatFileUrl/ChatFileUrlPart classes at chat.baml:263-273, constructed at :507-511 when resolve_media(pdf, false) leaves a URL.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat PDFs like audio: call ai.wire.resolve_media(pdf, true) so remote PDFs are fetched and inlined as file_data (data URL) + filename; delete ChatFileUrl/ChatFileUrlPart. (gs:// URLs would still error — acceptable, name it in the message.)

findings.claim: AzureClient's default api_version "2024-02-15-preview" is stale (Feb 2024 preview) and predates parameters the client itself exposes: per Azure's own api-version changelog, max_completion_tokens and stream_options.include_usage were only added in 2024-08/09-01-preview. A caller using the first-class max_completion_tokens field with the default api_version gets a service-side rejection/ignore. Azure's current guidance (since Aug 2025) is the v1 API ({resource}.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/ with NO api-version) or a GA dated version.
findings.evidence: learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/api-version-lifecycle: "api-version is no longer a required parameter with the v1 GA API"; changelog: "Changes between 2024-09-01-preview and 2024-08-01-preview: max_completion_tokens added… stream_options & include_usage added". Code: azure.baml:50 (default "2024-02-15-preview"), max_completion_tokens field at :41,60.
findings.suggested_fix: Default api_version to a current GA dated version (e.g. "2024-10-21" or newer), or better: support the v1 path ({resource}.openai.azure.com/openai/v1 + no api-version) as the default and keep dated api_version as the opt-in.

findings.claim: _chat_prune_nulls recurses through the ENTIRE serialized request, including tools[].function.parameters — the user's verbatim JSON Schema — so any legitimate null in a tool schema ("default": null, "const": null, nulls in nested option objects) is silently deleted from the wire, altering the schema the model sees and breaking strict-schema validation servers.
findings.evidence: Probe probe_tool_schema_null_loss: raw_tool with input_schema {"properties":{"x":{"type":["string","null"],"default":null}}} → captured body has default_key_present=false (key stripped). Code: chat_render_body chat.baml:955-958 runs _chat_prune_nulls (:746-765) over the whole body before the merge.
findings.suggested_fix: Prune nulls only at the ChatRequest top level (its optional fields) and within message objects the core built itself; never recurse into `tools[*].function.parameters` (and `request_body`-merged subtrees are already handled by _merge_json).

findings.claim: A stream truncated before finish_reason/[DONE] (server/proxy dies mid-answer) is returned as a SUCCESSFUL turn: partial text with StopReason.Complete and no error. The chat-completions wire contract has an explicit terminator ([DONE], and a finish_reason on the last content chunk) so the decoder can detect truncation, but never does; TurnStream's SSE-close-completes-the-turn fallback then reports silent data loss as success to require_done/Retry layers.
findings.evidence: Probe probe_truncated_stream: SSE serving one content delta then closing (no finish_reason, no [DONE]) → "par/Complete", no throw. Spec: openai-openapi stream_options.include_usage doc: chunks are "streamed before the `data: [DONE]` message"; decoder chat.baml:1239-1289 only pushes TurnDone on [DONE] and TurnMeta on finish_reason; ai/ns_stream/stream.baml TurnStream.next() returns Done on sse.next()==null with _stop_reason defaulting to Complete. Mitigating context: TurnDone's stdlib comment declares SSE-close-completes deliberate, but that generic fallback is wrong for a protocol with an explicit sentinel.
findings.suggested_fix: Track in ChatStreamDecoder whether finish_reason or [DONE] was seen; on stream end without either, throw ai.errors.NetworkFailure (retry-safety Unknown would be more honest if representable) or at minimum set a non-Complete stop reason.

findings.claim: PromptMessage.metadata is silently dropped by the entire chat-completions family: chat_lower_prompt never reads message.metadata (0 references in the file), so cache directives (OpenAI's documented per-part prompt_cache_breakpoint; OpenRouter's Anthropic-style cache_control) cannot reach the wire. PLAN §5 explicitly decided 'Message metadata placement (openai): engine (content part)' — an accepted decision to implement, not a §6 deferral — and the sibling Anthropic client DOES consume PromptMessage.metadata (cache_control), so the family is behind its own branch.
findings.evidence: grep metadata crates/baml_builtins2/baml_std/openai/ns_internal/chat.baml → 0 hits; anthropic/ns_internal/*.baml:311 reads message.metadata.get("cache_control"). ai/spec.baml:23-26 defines PromptMessage.metadata (from Role markers). openai-openapi@master: PromptCacheBreakpointParam is a property of every ChatCompletionRequestMessageContentPart* schema. PLAN.md §5 divergence table row 'Message metadata placement (openai) → engine (content part)'.
findings.suggested_fix: In chat_lower_prompt, forward recognized metadata keys onto the last content part of the lowered message (engine placement): prompt_cache_breakpoint for openai, cache_control for openrouter (gate by a ChatCompat flag or forward verbatim like anthropic does).

findings.claim: Image-by-URL is always passed through as a URL (resolve_media(image, false) hardcoded), but Ollama's OpenAI-compat docs state image URLs are NOT supported (base64 only) — so OllamaClient + Image.from_url sends a request Ollama cannot use, and neither ChatCompat nor any wrapper exposes an option to force inlining (sys_llm had the user-settable media_url_handler for exactly this; the parity matrix rows 'URL→base64 pre-resolution pass' / media_url_handler defaults are otherwise unimplemented in this family).
findings.evidence: docs.ollama.com/openai: vision support — 'Base64 encoded image ✓ / Image URL ✗'. Code: _chat_media_part chat.baml:485-491 uses ai.wire.resolve_media(image, false) unconditionally; ChatCompat (:40-108) has no media-inlining flag; research/openai-chat.md §5 row 'URL→base64 pre-resolution pass ✅ resolve_media.rs driven by media_url_handler'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a ChatCompat flag (e.g. inline_image_urls: bool, default false; true for OllamaClient) that makes _chat_media_part call resolve_media(image, true); optionally surface a per-client override field.

findings.claim: Streamed refusals are lost: the spec's ChatCompletionStreamResponseDelta has a `refusal` field, but CcDelta declares only role/content/reasoning_content/tool_calls, so a streamed refusal produces an empty final turn with no refusal text (the non-streaming path does surface message.refusal).
findings.evidence: openai-openapi@master ChatCompletionStreamResponseDelta properties include `refusal`; CcDelta at chat.baml:1165-1170 lacks it and decode (:1239-1289) never reads it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add refusal: string? to CcDelta and emit it as a TextDelta (mirroring the non-streaming path, which appends refusal as Text).

findings.claim: An unparseable SSE data payload is silently skipped (catch_all → null), so a corrupted chunk in the middle of a stream drops content without any signal; the engine surfaced unparsable SSE payloads as stream errors.
findings.evidence: Probe probe_malformed_sse: valid 'a' delta + truncated-JSON chunk + valid 'b' delta → "ab/Complete", no error, no log. Code chat.baml:1246-1250. Engine comparison: research/openai-chat.md §7 row 'unparsable SSE payload: surfaced as a stream error (stream_request.rs:104-116)'.
findings.suggested_fix: At minimum count skipped chunks and surface via log.warn or fold into a decoder flag that final_turn can report; or throw ParseFailed on unparseable non-[DONE] data.

findings.claim: tool_calls whose `arguments` string is not valid JSON silently degrade to args {} (both non-streaming parse and stream-assembled tool_uses), so the runner executes the tool with empty arguments and neither user nor model learns the arguments were discarded.
findings.evidence: Probe probe_bad_tool_args: canned response with arguments '{not json' → tool_uses = [t / {} / ToolUse]. Code: _chat_push_tool_uses chat.baml:1011-1017 and ChatStreamDecoder.tool_uses :1296-1302 both catch_all → empty map.
findings.suggested_fix: Throw ai.errors.ParseFailed (provider, raw_output=arguments) on undecodable arguments, or pass the raw string through under a reserved key so tool validation fails loudly.

findings.claim: classify_http receives only (status, body), so a 429's Retry-After response header is never captured: RateLimited.retry_after_ms is always null even though Backoff.delay_ms specifically honors that hint. The response headers are in scope at the _chat_send call site.
findings.evidence: errors.baml:124-137 signature classify_http(provider, status_code, body); chat.baml:1137-1139 calls it with response.status_code/text while response.headers is available; clients.baml Backoff comment: 'A root.errors.RateLimited.retry_after_ms hint overrides the computed value.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add an optional headers parameter (or a classify_http_with_headers overload) that parses Retry-After / retry-after-ms into RateLimited.retry_after_ms; wire it in _chat_send.

findings.claim: The audio-output modality is unreadable: CcMessage has no `audio` field, so a caller who requests audio output via request_body {"modalities":["text","audio"],"audio":{...}} (reachable through the sanctioned passthrough) gets message.audio.data silently dropped from the parsed turn.
findings.evidence: openai-openapi@master ChatCompletionResponseMessage includes `audio` (id/data/transcript/expires_at) for gpt-4o-audio models; CcMessage at chat.baml:404-413 reads content/images/reasoning_content/refusal/tool_calls only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add CcMessageAudio {id, data, transcript} to CcMessage and lower to ai.content.Media (Audio.from_base64) + Text(transcript), mirroring the images path.
